lines.en: Hi Omar! How did the job interview go yesterday?
Hi Sara. I was so nervous before it that I could not eat anything in the morning.
That is normal. Did they ask you the usual questions?
Yes. The interviewer asked me why I wanted to work for their company.
And what did you say?
I said I had read about the company and liked how it treats its employees.
Good answer. They told me they would call you by the end of the week, right?
Exactly. I am still waiting, and the waiting is the hardest part.
If you get the job, will you have to move closer to the office?
Maybe. But you do not have to decide that now. First, wait for the call.
True. By the way, are we still having the team meeting on Thursday?
It has been moved to Friday, because the manager is traveling.
If I cannot attend, should I let them know in advance?
Yes, at least one day before. And check your email, they sent the report attached.
I saw it. The email was so long that I could not read it to the end.
Nobody could. Next time they should keep it short.
Anyway, enough about work. Tell me about your dreams, Omar. What do you really want?
Ever since I was a child, I have dreamed of starting my own business.
That is a big ambition. Achieving it will take more than talent; it will take patience and daily effort.
I know. That is why I am saving money so that I can start next year.
Unless you try, you will never know how far you can go.
What about you? What is your biggest dream?
My biggest dream is not to be rich, but to do work that helps people.
That is beautiful. Do you think our jobs will still exist in twenty years?
Scientists say many of today's jobs will probably be done by machines by then.
Nobody knows what the future will bring, but we can prepare for it.
Exactly. Learning English is part of my preparation.
And mine too. One day we will look back and be proud of the journey.
I am sure we will. Take care, Omar, and good luck with the call.
Thanks, Sara. See you on Friday, at the meeting!
